derivation_notes: The quasi-static capacitor terminal voltage q/capacitance is refined to a rate-sensitive effective back-voltage by making the electrical restoring coefficient depend on the current loading over the dielectric relaxation timescale. This captures dielectric absorption phenomenologically without adding a new state, and it recovers the parent when polarization relaxes much faster than the LC motion or when |i| is small.
change_summary: The capacitor restoring term in di_dt is no longer determined only by q and capacitance; its effective stiffness is reduced during fast transients through a current-dependent factor tied to capacitance_relaxation_time. This creates same-q but different-di_dt curvature between slow and fast trajectory segments, consistent with polarization lag.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The effective capacitor is treated as quasi-static: once capacitance(t) is known, the capacitor voltage is fully determined by q/capacitance with no additional rate-dependent polarization contribution.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Dielectric absorption / polarization lag causes the capacitor's terminal voltage under rapid charge redistribution to depend on both stored charge and the instantaneous current, not only on the relaxed effective capacitance state.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: When capacitance_relaxation_time*Abs(i)/sqrt(inductance*small_signal_capacitance) << 1, the rate-sensitive factor tends to 1 and the parent capacitor term q/capacitance is recovered.

response_change.parent_relation: The capacitor contribution to di_dt is a single-valued restoring term -q/capacitance, so after capacitance is set by |q| the electrical restoring slope depends only on q and not on the instantaneous current direction or discharge rate.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the quasi-static capacitor law with a rate-sensitive capacitive back-voltage so the restoring contribution depends jointly on q and i, producing different effective electrical stiffness on charging versus discharging portions of the transient.
response_change.observable_effect: At comparable |q|, high-|i| segments show altered di_dt curvature and shifted peak-current decay relative to low-|i| segments; the parent cannot create this same-q, different-slope contrast because its capacitor voltage depends only on q/capacitance.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when capacitance_relaxation_time is comparable to or longer than the early LC timescale sqrt(inductance*small_signal_capacitance) and the release amplitude is large enough that both |q| and |i| become appreciable before the oscillation is strongly damped.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate release amplitudes already show mild mismatch between same-|q| segments with different |i|; in holdout, stronger releases amplify this rate-sensitive curvature difference without requiring a new intervention or changed initial-condition protocol.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the dielectric response to be quasi-static so the capacitor back-voltage depends only on q/capacitance and not on current-driven polarization lag.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: rate-sensitive dielectric back-voltage in a relaxing capacitor
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Dielectric absorption / polarization lag causes the capacitor's terminal voltage under rapid charge redistribution to depend on both stored charge and the instantaneous current, not only on the relaxed effective capacitance state.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the capacitor restoring contribution is no longer a fixed function of q once capacitance is known; its coefficient varies with current loading through a dimensionless timescale ratio, introducing a direct q-i interaction inside the scored target mapping.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The capacitor voltage entering di_dt is instantaneously q/capacitance once the capacitance state is specified.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The capacitor back-voltage is reduced during fast charge redistribution by dielectric polarization lag, implemented as a current-dependent coefficient on the restoring term.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: When capacitance_relaxation_time*Abs(i)/sqrt(inductance*small_signal_capacitance) << 1, the additional current-dependent factor approaches 1 and the parent expression is recovered.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Across trajectories generated with the same fixed parameters but different release amplitudes, compare time points with similar q and capacitance. The child predicts weaker electrical restoring action and therefore different di_dt curvature on high-|i| segments than on low-|i| segments, while the parent enforces the same capacitor contribution at those matched q and capacitance values.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all parent parameters cannot create this contrast with one shared parameter set because the parent capacitor law is structurally single-phase: once q and capacitance are matched, the capacitor contribution is fixed at -q/capacitance. Adjusting resistance, nonlinear resistance, inductance saturation, or capacitance-field parameters changes global i or q dependence, but none introduces the missing direct modulation of the capacitor restoring coefficient by instantaneous current.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when capacitance_relaxation_time is comparable to or longer than the early LC timescale sqrt(inductance*small_signal_capacitance) and the release amplitude is large enough that both |q| and |i| become appreciable before the oscillation is strongly damped.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate release amplitudes already show mild mismatch between same-|q| segments with different |i|; in holdout, stronger releases amplify this rate-sensitive curvature difference without requiring a new intervention or changed initial-condition protocol.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the dielectric response to be quasi-static so the capacitor back-voltage depends only on q/capacitance and not on current-driven polarization lag.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model lets capacitance relax in time but still assumes the capacitor voltage entering di_dt is instantaneously given by q/capacitance, omitting nonequilibrium dielectric back-voltage during fast polarization lag.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The effective capacitor is treated as quasi-static: once capacitance(t) is known, the capacitor voltage is fully determined by q/capacitance with no additional rate-dependent polarization contribution.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Dielectric absorption / polarization lag causes the capacitor's terminal voltage under rapid charge redistribution to depend on both stored charge and the instantaneous current, not only on the relaxed effective capacitance state.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's quasi-static capacitor assumption rather than adding a wholly new physical subsystem. The parent already includes dielectric relaxation through the capacitance state, but in the scored target mapping di_dt the capacitor enters only through -q/capacitance. That means two times during the transient with the same q and capacitance must produce the same electrical restoring contribution regardless of whether the capacitor is rapidly discharging or recharging. Scientifically, this is a shortcut: when dielectric polarization relaxes on a timescale comparable to the oscillation, the terminal capacitor voltage is not determined solely by q and the slowly evolving capacitance state. Vary the release amplitude so that one set of trajectories explores larger early |i| while holding the component parameters fixed. Under admissible conditions with capacitance_relaxation_time not much shorter than sqrt(inductance*small_signal_capacitance), the child model predicts a same-q but different-di_dt contrast between fast and slow segments because polarization lag modifies the restoring voltage according to current direction and magnitude. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce this across conditions: changing capacitance-field nonlinearity reshapes dependence on q, and changing inductive or resistive terms reshapes i effects globally, but the parent lacks a direct q-i interaction in the capacitor back-voltage itself. Limitation: if dielectric relaxation is extremely fast relative to the LC motion, the effect collapses and the parent remains adequate.

scenario_text: A series circuit containing an inductor, resistor, and capacitor is released from a charged initial state. The circuit current and capacitor charge exchange energy through the electric and magnetic storage elements while resistance removes energy. The baseline model uses fixed component values and excludes external driving after release.
